The sea pushes its first tongue of foam in through the gate and the moat takes it instantly, the surface climbing the cobalt-blue bucket buried rim-deep in the far wall.
The tall tower has slumped sideways and is still going, a crack running from its notched top all the way down to the wet cut face of the wall it stands on.
The upturned bucket, its scoured back turned toward the bright water, stands beside the sharp-edged turret it has just surrendered, wet dark sand still holding every ridge perfectly.
The water breaches the dam at its lowest point and races the length of the canal, the twelve bucket-cast turrets lining the far side trembling in the pressure wave rolling past them.
A herring gull stands dead centre in the top court on one yellow foot, facing the incoming tide, and has not moved an inch.
The shovel, buried to its socket in the last gap of the parapet with only its sun-yellowed handle above the wall top, holds the gap closed while the wet sand sets hard around its blade.
A green plastic soldier stands on the highest turret, facing the water, the wet sand packed into the grooves along its rifle already beginning to dry pale against its cobalt coat.
The canal's near side gives way all at once, and the water cuts itself a new route through the freshly collapsed sand, the old straight line already half gone.
Three sandpipers run the full length of the moat one ahead and two abreast behind, their tracks stitched into the wet floor of it in two parallel rows of fine three-pronged prints.
A small plastic dinosaur stands on the dam, vermilion against the dark wet sand, and the water is already past its feet and climbing the far face of the dam below it.
The top turret has dried to pale amber and is shedding steadily down its own flank, a thin stream of loose grains collecting in a low heap against the shovel handle propped beside it.
The water arrives down two canals at once and the two fronts meet head-on in the middle pool, the surface surging upward between them and spreading toward every wall at once.
A small green crab has moved into the doorway of the tallest tower and sits in it facing out, one claw raised, the wet sand floor of the doorway already pressed with its neat claw-prints.
The driftwood plank lies newly across the moat, its grey ends bedding themselves into the ochre sand on both sides, the water below it running dark and fast in the shadow it throws.
The dam is holding but weeping in four places at once, four thin lines of bright water running down its seaward face and pooling at its base where the sand is already going soft.
Water finds a hollow in the base of the outer wall and pours clean out of the far side of it, the wall above the hole still standing, still solid, entirely unaware.
The tide's first reach touches the outer wall and stops just short of it, the wet-dark line sitting a shovel-blade from the wall's base, the dry sand between them still holding its colour.
A plastic knight lies on its side on the ramp, half-buried under the sand that came down with the wall above him, one gauntleted fist still raised above the surface.
The moat has filled above the level of the canal feeding it and the water is now running backwards up the canal, the flow reversed, the far end of the canal beginning to flood.
The rake's parallel grooves run dead straight across the sand and end exactly at the water's edge, the last groove filled with bright water to the brim and perfectly level.
A die-cast digger sits in the spoil heap at the end of the trench, its blade packed with wet terracotta sand and its tracks half-buried in the mound it has spent the day building.
A whole stretch of the near wall has fallen in, and the sand is still sliding, grains running in slow streams down the broken cut face and fanning across the canal floor below.
A line of dog paw-prints goes straight up the ramp, over the top of the parapet, and down the far side into the top court, the deep prints on the ramp already beginning to fill with water.
An oystercatcher stands on the highest point of the dam on one orange leg, its bill tucked in, the wet sand around both its feet darkening as the water rises through it from below.

Water finds the rabbit-hole at the base of the seaward tower and pours through it, emerging from the courtyard side in a wide fan across the cobalt-packed sand floor, bright and fast and already spreading.
